answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying every identity to a locked stake, which acts as a bridge between reputation and real cost: to join, an agent must deposit value, and misbehaviour forfeits it, so spinning up thousands of fakes costs thousands of deposits. Reputation works like a cedar growing slowly - it accrues only through a verifiable history of honest work, so a fresh identity carries no weight. A plume of signals, such as uptime proofs and peer attestations, lets the network grant small jobs first and larger ones only after trust is earned.
